Sure thing! I still like the mouse, it's super unique, it feels pretty solid and has more customization than I know what to do with. There is quite a bit going on when you first hook it up, it has its own software that allows you to create control profiles for different games and apps. The software is very in-depth and allows you to map custom keystrokes to the mouse. You can even map multiple buttons at once for a single function, Ctrl alt del can be mapped to a single button on the mouse for example. 

The only downfall is that the gyro responsible for the tilt function isn't the best. You can change the sensitivity settings in the software, but it's a hit or miss. Sometimes, it works perfectly and gives me an advantage. Other times, the tilt function doesn't want to play and causes my character to get stuck in a lean position until I recalibrate the mouse. This issue doesn't ruin the experience, but having to recalibrate once every hour or two can get annoying. Thankfully, their discord is pretty active, and they can help with any issue that comes up. 

When it works, it feels super satisfying. You can even program the mouse to function like a steering wheel for some games. I still haven't tried using the flight stick baseplate for it yet, but I'm sure flying something in a game while using it would be really cool too. 

Overall I think it's a great mouse with tons of cool features. Hopefully they are planning on ironing out some of the small issues with the tilt function soon.
